exposure: Maternal self-reported use of nicotine-containing products in pregnancy (any nicotine exposure)
Cigarette smoking with or without other nicotine-containing products in pregnancy
outcome: Infant lung function (risk of a ratio of time to peak tidal expiratory flow to total expiratory time <25th percentile)
cohort: The study included 1163 infants from the Scandinavian population-based Preventing Atopic Dermatitis and ALLergies in Children birth cohort with available tidal flow-volume measurements at 3 months of age and maternal self-reported use of nicotine-containing products in pregnancy.
finding: In utero exposure to nicotine-containing products, including snus and cigarettes, was associated with a higher risk of lower lung function in infancy.
